methodology.centrality: Geometric mean of distinct indexed scholarly-work counts for the mapped measures. Surveys included; web missions, notes, derived claims and citation-only proof_sources excluded. Definition/notation references, direct checked comparison records and explicitly annotated measure mentions in question passages supply the evidence. Counts are lower counts within this corpus, not a full-text census.
methodology.recurrence: Distinct works with a curated passage discussing this same question; survey and research counts shown separately. Paper versions count once. Bound citations alone are not question mentions.
methodology.implication_reach: Number of improved ordered core upper-bound comparisons under the stated hypothetical pure bound, preserving scope. Not assessed for unsupported models or nonrational target endpoints.
methodology.gap: Upper exponent minus lower exponent, only when both finite endpoints are recorded. Endpoint losses are listed separately and have no exponent-gap score.
methodology.recent: Latest year of a recorded substantive source, formulation or bound in the entry. Access dates are not activity dates.
methodology.longevity: Earliest formulation year verified in the listed question passages; inferred gaps have no historical origin assigned.
methodology.missing: Missing or inapplicable ranking values are null, displayed as not assessed and sorted last. There is no combined importance score.
methodology.scope_warning: Centrality may be compared across domains, but mathematical bounds and conditional implications never transfer across domains without recorded evidence.
methodology.version_policy: Merge exact normalized titles and explicitly audited version families; this is a conservative editorial work index, available for inspection.

formulation_audit.fixed_sign_completion: If F is required to equal sign(p) off the promise, existence of some other low-degree completion does not imply this fixed F is easy. Kernel preservation on the promise does not establish off-promise sign agreement.

uniformity_and_norm_audit.bounded_target_coefficients: For globally bounded p and q, each Fourier coefficient has magnitude at most one, so unrestricted Delta=qhat-phat has coefficient infinity norm at most two.
